name: Land Surveyor (KEA)
description: KEA/KPSC Karnataka Land Surveyor (RPC) — Paper-I general knowledge and Paper-II survey methods, physics, mathematics and computer applications.

questions.question: A Gunter's chain used in land surveying is how long?
questions.explanation: Gunter's chain is 66 feet long and divided into 100 links, which makes 10 square chains exactly one acre. The engineer's chain is 100 feet, and metric chains are 20 or 30 metres.

questions.question: If a chain used for measurement is too long, the measured length of a line will be
questions.explanation: A chain that is too long covers more ground per chain-length, so fewer chain-lengths are counted and the measured value comes out smaller than the truth. The true length is therefore greater, which is why the correction is added.

questions.question: In chain surveying, the process of establishing intermediate points on a survey line is called
questions.explanation: Ranging fixes intermediate points on the straight line between two stations so that the chain can be laid accurately. Offsetting measures lateral distances to detail from that line.

questions.question: In a metric chain of 20 metres, how many links are there?
questions.explanation: A 20 metre metric chain has 100 links, so each link is 0.2 metre. The 30 metre metric chain has 150 links of the same 0.2 metre size.

questions.question: Which offset is measured at right angles to the survey line?
questions.explanation: A perpendicular offset is taken at right angles to the chain line, usually with a cross staff or optical square. An oblique offset is taken at any other angle and needs two measurements to fix the point.

questions.question: A prismatic compass is graduated from 0° to 360° in which system of bearings?
questions.explanation: The prismatic compass reads whole circle bearings from 0° to 360° measured clockwise from north. The surveyor's compass instead reads quadrantal or reduced bearings from 0° to 90° in each quadrant.

questions.question: The horizontal angle between the true meridian and the magnetic meridian is called
questions.explanation: Magnetic declination is the angle between true north and magnetic north at a place. Dip is the vertical angle the needle makes with the horizontal, and local attraction is a disturbance from nearby iron.

questions.question: The whole circle bearing of a line is 210°. Its reduced bearing is
questions.explanation: A bearing between 180° and 270° lies in the third quadrant, so the reduced bearing is measured from south towards west as WCB minus 180°, giving S 30° W.

questions.question: Local attraction in compass surveying is detected by checking that
options: The fore and back bearings of a line differ by exactly 180°
The sum of all interior angles equals 360°
The needle points to true north
questions.explanation: For an undisturbed line the fore bearing and back bearing must differ by exactly 180°. A departure from that difference shows one or both stations are affected by local attraction.

questions.question: Which accessory of a plane table is used for sighting objects and drawing the ray?
questions.explanation: The alidade carries the sight vanes and its bevelled edge draws the ray on the sheet. The plumbing fork centres the table over the ground station and the trough compass orients it to magnetic north.

questions.question: Which plane table method is used to locate the position of the table itself from two or more already-plotted points?
questions.explanation: Resection fixes the instrument station by sighting points that are already plotted. Radiation and intersection instead plot new detail from a known station, and traversing runs a connected series of lines.

questions.question: The three-point problem in plane tabling is solved by which of these methods?
questions.explanation: Bessel's graphical method, along with the tracing paper and trial-and-error methods, solves the three-point problem. Bowditch's rule adjusts traverse closing error and the rise and fall method reduces level readings.

questions.question: In levelling, a benchmark is best described as
options: A staff reading taken on a turning point
questions.explanation: A benchmark is a fixed reference point whose elevation is known relative to a datum. Height of instrument and staff readings are values computed or observed during the work, not fixed references.

questions.question: The first staff reading taken after setting up a level on a point of known elevation is called
questions.explanation: A back sight is the first reading after setting up, taken on a point of known elevation to establish the height of the instrument. A fore sight is the last reading before shifting the instrument.

questions.question: In the height of instrument method of reducing levels, the height of instrument equals
options: Reduced level of the point plus back sight
questions.explanation: Height of instrument is the reduced level of the benchmark plus the back sight taken on it, and the reduced level of any other point is then that height minus the staff reading there.

questions.question: In the rise and fall method, the arithmetic check is that the sum of back sights minus the sum of fore sights equals
options: The sum of rises minus the sum of falls, and the last reduced level minus the first
questions.explanation: All three quantities must agree: the difference of back and fore sight totals, the difference of rise and fall totals, and the difference between the last and first reduced levels. Any mismatch signals an arithmetic error.

questions.question: Which type of level has a telescope rigidly fixed to its vertical spindle?
questions.explanation: In a dumpy level the telescope is rigidly attached so it cannot be tilted independently. A tilting level allows small tilts of the telescope, and an automatic level uses a compensator to level the line of sight.

questions.question: A contour line on a map joins points of equal
questions.explanation: A contour joins points at the same elevation above a datum. The spacing between contours indicates slope, but the line itself is defined by constant height.

questions.question: Contour lines that are closely spaced on a map indicate
questions.explanation: Close spacing means a large change of height over a short horizontal distance, which is a steep slope. Widely spaced contours indicate gentle ground, and equally spaced ones a uniform slope.

questions.question: Two contour lines of different elevation can cross each other only in the case of
questions.explanation: Contours normally never cross, because one ground point cannot have two elevations. An overhanging cliff or cave is the sole exception, where rock lies above ground of a different height.

questions.question: A theodolite whose telescope can be revolved through 180° in a vertical plane about its horizontal axis is called a
questions.explanation: A transit theodolite allows the telescope to be reversed, or transited, through the vertical plane. Non-transit instruments cannot do this, which limits the checks available to the observer.

questions.question: Observing a horizontal angle on both face left and face right chiefly eliminates
options: Instrumental errors of collimation and trunnion axis
questions.explanation: Taking the mean of face left and face right readings cancels instrumental errors such as line of collimation and trunnion axis misalignment, because they act with opposite sign on the two faces.

questions.question: Bowditch's rule is used in traverse computation to
options: Distribute the closing error in latitudes and departures
Compute the area of a plot
questions.explanation: Bowditch's or the compass rule distributes closing error in proportion to the lengths of the traverse legs. Transit rule distributes it in proportion to latitudes and departures instead.

questions.question: The multiplying constant of an ordinary stadia tacheometer is usually taken as
questions.explanation: The multiplying constant is normally 100, so the horizontal distance is about 100 times the staff intercept. The additive constant is small and often nearly zero in anallatic instruments.

questions.question: A total station combines a theodolite with which additional instrument?
questions.explanation: A total station integrates an electronic theodolite with an EDM and a data recorder, so angles and distances are captured together. It replaces the separate chain and theodolite workflow.

questions.question: Electronic distance measurement instruments determine distance principally by measuring
options: The travel time or phase shift of an electromagnetic wave
The angle subtended by a staff
questions.explanation: EDM sends a modulated light or microwave signal to a reflector and derives the distance from the return travel time or phase difference. Staff intercepts belong to tacheometry, not EDM.

questions.question: The Global Positioning System fixes a receiver's position using which principle?
questions.explanation: A GPS receiver measures its distance to several satellites and solves for position by trilateration, needing at least four satellites to resolve position and clock error together.

questions.question: India's own satellite navigation system is known as
questions.explanation: NavIC, from the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System, is developed by ISRO. GLONASS is Russian, Galileo European and BeiDou Chinese.

questions.question: In a geographic information system, data represented as a grid of cells is called
questions.explanation: Raster data stores information in a grid of cells or pixels, suited to continuous surfaces. Vector data uses points, lines and polygons, which suits discrete features such as parcel boundaries.

questions.question: A remote sensing system that supplies its own energy source, such as radar, is described as
questions.explanation: Active systems emit their own radiation and record what returns, so they work at night and through cloud. Passive systems such as ordinary optical sensors depend on reflected sunlight.

questions.question: The Survey of India, the country's national mapping agency, has its headquarters at
questions.explanation: The Survey of India is headquartered at Dehradun. Hyderabad hosts the National Remote Sensing Centre, which handles satellite data rather than national mapping.

questions.question: The Great Trigonometrical Survey of India was begun in 1802 under the direction of
questions.explanation: William Lambton started the Great Trigonometrical Survey in 1802 and George Everest carried it forward as his successor. James Rennell was the first Surveyor General of Bengal, decades earlier.

questions.question: The SI unit of force is the
questions.explanation: One newton is the force that accelerates one kilogram at one metre per second squared. The joule is energy, the watt power, and the pascal pressure.

questions.question: Which quantity is a vector?
questions.explanation: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector. Speed is the magnitude of velocity alone, and mass and temperature are scalars.

questions.question: The bending of light as it passes from air into water is called
questions.explanation: Refraction is the change of direction caused by a change in the speed of light between media. Reflection returns light from a surface, and dispersion separates it into colours.

questions.question: According to Newton's second law, the net force on a body equals
options: The rate of change of its momentum
questions.explanation: The second law states that force is the rate of change of momentum, which reduces to mass times acceleration when mass is constant. Mass times velocity is momentum itself, not force.

questions.question: The area of a triangle with base 12 cm and height 5 cm is
questions.explanation: The area is half the base times the height, so half of 12 times 5 gives 30 square centimetres. Sixty would be the answer if the halving were forgotten.

questions.question: In a right-angled triangle the sides are 9 cm and 12 cm about the right angle. The hypotenuse is
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras the hypotenuse is the square root of 81 plus 144, which is the square root of 225, or 15 centimetres. Adding the sides directly would wrongly give 21.

questions.question: One hectare is equal to how many square metres?
questions.explanation: A hectare is a square of 100 metres a side, so 10,000 square metres. It is roughly 2.47 acres, and is the standard unit in Indian land records alongside the acre and guntha.

questions.question: If the sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 1080°, the polygon has how many sides?
questions.explanation: The sum of interior angles is 180 times two less than the number of sides. Setting that equal to 1080 gives six for the bracket, so the polygon has eight sides.

questions.question: In computing, which of these is an example of system software?
questions.explanation: An operating system manages the hardware and provides services to other programs, which makes it system software. Spreadsheets, browsers and image editors are application software running on top of it.

questions.question: One kilobyte is conventionally taken as how many bytes?
questions.explanation: In the binary convention used for memory, a kilobyte is 2 to the power 10, or 1024 bytes. Storage manufacturers often use the decimal 1000, which is why advertised disk capacity looks smaller once formatted.

questions.question: Which type of computer memory loses its contents when power is switched off?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile and clears when power is removed. ROM, hard disks and flash memory all retain data without power, which is why programs are stored there and loaded into RAM to run.

questions.question: India's Five-Year Plans were formulated by which body until it was replaced in 2015?
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission drew up the Five-Year Plans from 1950 until NITI Aayog replaced it in 2015. The Finance Commission is a separate constitutional body dealing with tax devolution.

questions.question: The Union Budget of India is presented in Parliament under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 112 provides for the annual financial statement, commonly called the Budget. Article 110 defines a Money Bill, 265 bars taxation without authority of law, and 280 sets up the Finance Commission.

questions.question: Which award is India's highest civilian honour?
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award, ahead of the Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri. The Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime military decoration.

questions.question: In chain surveying, a tie line is used mainly to
options: Check the accuracy of the survey and locate interior detail
questions.explanation: A tie or check line connects two known points on other lines, so its measured length can be compared with its plotted length as a proof of accuracy.

questions.question: The correction for sag in a suspended tape is always
questions.explanation: A sagging tape follows a curve longer than the straight line between supports, so the measured value is too large and the correction is subtracted.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to set out a perpendicular offset from a chain line?
questions.explanation: A cross staff or optical square sights at right angles to the chain line. A compass measures bearings and a level measures heights.

questions.question: The correction for slope when measuring along sloping ground is
questions.explanation: A distance measured along a slope is longer than its horizontal projection, so the slope correction is always subtracted to get plan distance.

questions.question: If a 20 m chain is 5 cm too short, the true length of a line measured as 400 m is
questions.explanation: True length is measured length times the ratio of actual to nominal chain length, so 400 times 19.95 divided by 20 gives 399 m. A short chain over-reads.

questions.question: In a prismatic compass the graduated ring is attached to
options: The magnetic needle, so the ring stays fixed while the box turns
The box, so it turns with the sight vanes
questions.explanation: In a prismatic compass the ring is fixed to the needle and remains oriented to magnetic north while the box rotates, which is why it reads whole circle bearings directly.

questions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is 45 degrees and the declination is 2 degrees west. The true bearing is
questions.explanation: With westerly declination the magnetic north lies west of true north, so the true bearing is the magnetic bearing minus the declination.

questions.question: A closed traverse is one in which the survey lines
options: Form a closed polygon or return to the starting point
questions.explanation: A closed traverse returns to its origin or to a second known point, which allows the closing error to be computed. An open traverse gives no such check.

questions.question: Local attraction is caused by
options: Nearby iron objects or electric currents deflecting the needle
questions.explanation: Iron railings, steel structures and power lines deflect the compass needle locally. The fore and back bearing check is how such stations are detected.

questions.question: A change point in levelling is a point on which
options: Both a fore sight and a back sight are taken
Only an intermediate sight is taken
questions.explanation: A change or turning point carries the level forward: the fore sight from the old setup and the back sight from the new one are both read on it.

questions.question: The collimation error of a level is best eliminated by
options: Balancing back sight and fore sight distances
questions.explanation: An equal-distance setup makes the collimation error affect both readings equally, so it cancels in the difference. This is the reciprocal levelling principle.

questions.question: Reciprocal levelling is used when
options: A river or valley prevents equal sight distances
The staff is shorter than usual
questions.explanation: When an obstacle forces unequal sights, observing from both banks and averaging cancels collimation, curvature and refraction errors.

questions.question: The effect of the earth's curvature on a long level sight makes the reading
options: Too large, so the correction is subtractive
Too small, so the correction is additive
questions.explanation: Curvature drops the level surface away from the horizontal line of sight, so the staff reads high and the correction is subtracted. Refraction partly offsets it.

questions.question: In profile levelling, the reduced levels are plotted against
questions.explanation: A longitudinal section plots reduced level against chainage, giving the ground profile along a road, canal or pipeline alignment.

questions.question: The vertical distance between two consecutive contours is called the
questions.explanation: The contour interval is the constant vertical spacing. The horizontal distance between the same two contours is the horizontal equivalent, which varies with slope.

questions.question: Contours that close on themselves with progressively lower values towards the centre indicate a
questions.explanation: Concentric contours decreasing inward describe a hollow. Increasing inward would describe a hill, which is why depression contours carry hachure marks on maps.

questions.question: Contour lines crossing a stream valley form which shape, pointing which way?
questions.explanation: Contours bend upstream as they cross a valley because the valley floor is lower, so the same elevation is reached further inland along the channel.

questions.question: The temporary adjustments of a theodolite are setting up, levelling and
questions.explanation: Temporary adjustments are made at every setup: centring, levelling and focusing the eyepiece and objective so the cross hairs and image do not shift relative to each other.

questions.question: The method of repetition in theodolite work is used to
options: Improve the accuracy of a measured horizontal angle
questions.explanation: Repetition accumulates the same angle several times on the circle and divides by the number of repetitions, reducing reading and graduation errors.

questions.question: In traverse computation, latitude of a line is its projection on the
questions.explanation: Latitude is the north-south component, computed as length times cosine of the bearing. Departure is the east-west component, using the sine.

questions.question: In a closed traverse, the algebraic sum of the latitudes should theoretically be
questions.explanation: Returning to the starting point means the northings and southings cancel, so both the latitude and departure sums should be zero. Any residue is the closing error.

questions.question: Tacheometry is used chiefly where
options: Direct chaining is difficult, such as broken or steep ground
questions.explanation: Tacheometry derives distance from a staff intercept rather than a tape, which suits steep, wooded or waterlogged ground where chaining is impractical.

questions.question: In the stadia system, if the staff intercept is 1.5 m and the multiplying constant is 100, the horizontal distance on a level sight is about
questions.explanation: Distance is the intercept times the multiplying constant plus the small additive constant, giving roughly 150 m for a 1.5 m intercept.

questions.question: In a total station, angles and distances are recorded
options: Electronically, and can be downloaded without manual booking
questions.explanation: A total station stores observations digitally, which removes the transcription errors that hand booking introduces and speeds up plotting.

questions.question: Differential GPS improves accuracy by using
options: A base station at a known point to correct the rover's position
questions.explanation: DGPS computes the error at a base station whose coordinates are known and applies that correction to the rover, cancelling most atmospheric and orbital error.

questions.question: How many satellites must a GPS receiver observe to fix a three-dimensional position?
questions.explanation: Three satellites fix three coordinates, and a fourth is needed to solve the receiver clock error, which is why four is the practical minimum.

questions.question: Spatial resolution of a satellite image refers to
options: The ground area represented by one pixel
questions.explanation: Spatial resolution is the ground size of a pixel. Spectral resolution counts the bands, temporal resolution the revisit interval, and radiometric the bit depth.

questions.question: In GIS, overlaying a cadastral parcel layer on a soil layer to find which soils fall in a parcel is an example of
questions.explanation: Overlay analysis combines two spatial layers to answer a question neither can alone. Georeferencing merely fixes an image to real-world coordinates.

questions.question: The datum for levelling in India is referenced to mean sea level determined at
options: Tide gauge observations at several ports, historically including Karachi
questions.explanation: The Indian levelling datum was derived from tide gauge observations, and Survey of India benchmarks carry heights above that mean sea level surface.

questions.question: The SI unit of pressure is the
questions.explanation: One pascal is one newton per square metre. The newton is force, the joule energy and the watt power.

questions.question: Which quantity remains constant when a body moves with uniform velocity?
options: Kinetic energy only in one direction
questions.explanation: Uniform velocity means no acceleration, so by Newton's first law the net force is zero and momentum stays constant.

questions.question: A body is in equilibrium when
options: The vector sum of forces and of moments about any point are both zero
Only the forces sum to zero
Only the moments sum to zero
It is at rest at the origin
questions.explanation: Static equilibrium requires both conditions: zero resultant force prevents translation and zero resultant moment prevents rotation.

questions.question: The bending of a surveying staff image seen through hot air near the ground is due to
questions.explanation: Temperature gradients change air density and bend the light path, which is why long sights close to hot ground are avoided in precise levelling.

questions.question: The area of a circle of radius 7 cm is approximately
questions.explanation: Area is pi times the radius squared, so 22/7 times 49 gives 154 square centimetres. Forty-four would be the circumference instead.

questions.question: One acre is approximately how many square metres?
questions.explanation: An acre is about 4047 square metres, roughly 0.4 hectare. Ten thousand square metres is a full hectare.

questions.question: In a right-angled triangle, if one acute angle is 30 degrees, the side opposite it is what fraction of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: The sine of 30 degrees is one half, so the opposite side is half the hypotenuse. This is the standard 30-60-90 ratio.

questions.question: If a plot measures 40 m by 25 m, its area in hectares is
questions.explanation: The area is 1000 square metres, and a hectare is 10,000 square metres, so the plot is 0.1 hectare.

questions.question: The simple interest on 8000 rupees at 5 percent for 3 years is
questions.explanation: Simple interest is principal times rate times time divided by 100, giving 8000 times 5 times 3 over 100, which is 1200.

questions.question: In a computer, which component executes arithmetic and logic operations?
questions.explanation: The arithmetic logic unit within the processor performs calculations and comparisons. Storage and display devices hold or present data rather than compute it.

questions.question: Which file format is commonly used to exchange survey coordinate data as plain text?
questions.explanation: Comma-separated values hold point number, northing, easting and elevation as readable text that almost any software can import.

questions.question: Which organisation prepares India's topographical maps?
questions.explanation: The Survey of India produces the national topographical map series. The Geological Survey maps rocks and minerals instead.

questions.question: Which of these is a cumulative error in chain surveying?
options: Using a chain of incorrect length
questions.explanation: A wrong chain length errs the same way every time, so the error accumulates with distance. Careless holding and reading vary in sign and tend to compensate.

questions.question: Reciprocal ranging is needed when
options: The two ends of a line are not intervisible
questions.explanation: When a hill hides one end from the other, two surveyors direct each other into line by successive approximation until both are on the straight line.

questions.question: The temperature correction for a steel tape used above its standardisation temperature is
questions.explanation: A warmer tape is longer than nominal, so each tape length covers more ground and the measured value is too small; the correction is added.

questions.question: Which is the most suitable survey method for a small, fairly level area with few details?
questions.explanation: Chain surveying suits small, open and reasonably level ground. Undulating or large areas need instruments that measure angles or use aerial and satellite data.

questions.question: An offset longer than about 15 metres is generally taken as
options: An oblique offset with two measurements
questions.explanation: Beyond a short distance a right angle cannot be judged accurately, so the point is fixed by two oblique measurements from known chainages instead.

questions.question: The angle between two survey lines computed from their whole circle bearings is called the
questions.explanation: The included angle at a station is the difference of the bearings of the two lines meeting there. A deflection angle is measured from the prolongation of the previous line.

questions.question: If the fore bearing of a line is 120 degrees, its back bearing is
questions.explanation: Back bearing is fore bearing plus 180 degrees when the fore bearing is under 180, giving 300 degrees here.

questions.question: A surveyor's compass differs from a prismatic compass in that it reads
options: Quadrantal bearings from 0 to 90 in each quadrant
questions.explanation: The surveyor's compass gives reduced or quadrantal bearings measured from north or south towards east or west, unlike the prismatic compass's 0 to 360 reading.

questions.question: Magnetic declination at a place changes over time mainly because of
options: Slow movement of the earth's magnetic poles
questions.explanation: Secular variation from the drifting magnetic field alters declination over years, which is why old bearings must be corrected before reuse.

questions.question: The main advantage of plane tabling is that
options: The plan is drawn in the field while the ground is in view
It gives the highest possible precision
It works well in heavy rain
questions.explanation: Plotting on site means omissions are noticed immediately. Its weaknesses are lower precision and being unusable in wet weather.

questions.question: Orienting a plane table by backsighting along a previously drawn line is more accurate than using the trough compass because
options: It is unaffected by local attraction
It works without a known station
questions.explanation: A compass needle can be deflected by nearby iron, while backsighting depends only on the geometry already plotted.

questions.question: In the radiation method of plane tabling, detail points are located by
options: Drawing rays from one station and scaling measured distances
questions.explanation: Radiation plots each point along its ray at the measured distance from a single station, which suits small areas within tape range.

questions.question: An inverted staff reading, used for the underside of a bridge or a ceiling, is entered in the level book as
questions.explanation: The point is above the line of collimation, so the reading is booked negative and the usual arithmetic then gives the correct reduced level.

questions.question: Which levelling method is best for checking a long line of levels for error?
options: Fly levelling back to the starting benchmark
questions.explanation: Closing the circuit back onto the starting benchmark reveals the accumulated misclosure, which can then be distributed. Intermediate sights add detail but no check.

questions.question: A bench mark established by the Survey of India as part of the national network is called a
questions.explanation: Great Trigonometrical Survey benchmarks carry precise heights above mean sea level. Temporary and arbitrary marks are local to one job.

questions.question: In the height of instrument method, an arithmetic check is that the sum of back sights minus the sum of fore sights equals
options: The last reduced level minus the first
questions.explanation: This difference must equal the net rise or fall over the whole line. Any mismatch signals a booking or arithmetic error, not a field error.

questions.question: A contour interval is usually chosen based on
options: The scale of the map, the terrain and the purpose
questions.explanation: Flat ground and large scales take a small interval; steep ground or small scales take a larger one, or the contours would be unreadably dense.

questions.question: Equally spaced contours on a map indicate
questions.explanation: Constant horizontal equivalent means the ground rises at a constant rate. Converging contours mean a steepening slope.

questions.question: Which method of contouring is called the indirect method?
options: Locating spot levels on a grid and interpolating contours
Tracing each contour on the ground
Following the water line of a reservoir
questions.explanation: The indirect method levels a grid of points and interpolates the contours on paper, which is far quicker than physically tracing each contour on site.

questions.question: Which permanent adjustment ensures the line of collimation is perpendicular to the horizontal axis?
options: Adjustment of the line of sight
questions.explanation: If the line of sight is not perpendicular to the trunnion axis, the telescope traces a cone rather than a plane, and the error is eliminated by the two-peg or face-change method.

questions.question: The closing error of a traverse is distributed by the transit rule in proportion to
options: The latitudes and departures of each line
questions.explanation: The transit rule apportions error by the size of each latitude and departure, while Bowditch's rule uses the line lengths. Transit suits traverses where angles are more reliable than distances.

questions.question: A deflection angle traverse is most commonly used for
options: Long narrow routes such as roads, canals and railways
questions.explanation: Route surveys run largely in one direction, so measuring the deflection from the previous line's prolongation is the natural way to record the alignment.

questions.question: The vertical angle measured above the horizontal is called the
questions.explanation: Elevation is measured upward and depression downward from the horizontal. Azimuth and bearing are horizontal directions.

questions.question: An anallatic lens in a tacheometer is used to
options: Make the additive constant effectively zero
questions.explanation: The anallatic lens shifts the apparent origin of measurement to the instrument's vertical axis, so distance is simply the intercept times 100.

questions.question: When a tacheometric sight is inclined, the staff intercept must be corrected because
options: The staff is not perpendicular to the line of sight
questions.explanation: A vertical staff meets an inclined sight obliquely, so the intercept is larger than it would be perpendicular; the correction uses the cosine of the vertical angle.

questions.question: In a total station survey, a prism is used to
options: Return the EDM signal to the instrument
questions.explanation: A corner-cube prism reflects the beam back along its incoming path regardless of small tilts, which is why it works at long ranges.

questions.question: Multipath error in GPS is caused by
options: Signals reflecting off buildings or water before reaching the antenna
questions.explanation: A reflected signal travels further than the direct one, biasing the range. Choosing open sites and using choke-ring antennas reduces it.

questions.question: Real time kinematic GPS achieves centimetre accuracy by using
options: Carrier phase measurements with corrections from a base station
questions.explanation: RTK resolves the carrier phase ambiguity using base station corrections sent in real time, which is far more precise than code ranging alone.

questions.question: Which platform gives the highest spatial resolution for a small site survey?
options: A drone flying a few hundred metres up
questions.explanation: Ground sample distance falls with altitude, so a low-flying drone resolves centimetres where satellites resolve metres.

questions.question: A digital elevation model represents
options: Terrain height as a grid or network of elevation values
questions.explanation: A DEM stores elevation across an area, from which slope, aspect, watersheds and contours can all be derived.

questions.question: Which projection is used for the Survey of India topographical map series?
options: Lambert conformal conic and polyconic historically
questions.explanation: India's topographical sheets have historically used polyconic and later Lambert conformal conic projections, chosen to limit distortion over the country's latitude range.

questions.question: A scale of 1:50,000 means one centimetre on the map represents
questions.explanation: One centimetre times 50,000 is 50,000 centimetres, which is 500 metres.

questions.question: The density of pure water at 4 degrees Celsius is approximately
questions.explanation: Water is densest near 4 degrees Celsius at about 1000 kilograms per cubic metre, which is one gram per cubic centimetre.

questions.question: Which instrument measures atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures pressure, a hygrometer humidity, an anemometer wind speed and an ammeter electric current.

questions.question: The acceleration due to gravity is approximately
questions.explanation: Standard gravity is about 9.81 metres per second squared. Metres per second alone would be a speed, not an acceleration.

questions.question: Work done is zero when the force acting on a body is
questions.explanation: Work is force times displacement times the cosine of the angle between them, and the cosine of ninety degrees is zero.

questions.question: The volume of a cube of side 5 cm is
questions.explanation: Volume is the side cubed, so five times five times five gives 125 cubic centimetres. Twenty-five would be the area of one face.

questions.question: If 3 workers finish a task in 12 days, how long will 6 workers take, working at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Work is inversely proportional to the number of workers, so doubling them halves the time.

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 60 m and its length is twice its breadth. Its area is
questions.explanation: With length 2b, the perimeter 6b equals 60 so b is 10 and the length 20, giving an area of 200 square metres.

questions.question: What is 15 percent of 400?
questions.explanation: Fifteen percent is 15 divided by 100, times 400, which gives 60.

questions.question: One guntha, a land unit used in Karnataka, is approximately how many square metres?
questions.explanation: A guntha is about 101 square metres, and forty gunthas make one acre of roughly 4047 square metres.

questions.question: Which software category would AutoCAD belong to for a surveyor?
questions.explanation: CAD software draws and edits plans and sections from survey coordinates, which is the surveyor's main drafting tool.

questions.question: A backup of survey data should ideally be kept
options: In more than one location, including off site
questions.explanation: A single copy is lost with the device that holds it. Keeping a second copy elsewhere is what protects against theft, damage and drive failure.

questions.question: Which Indian organisation is responsible for weather forecasting?
questions.explanation: The IMD issues forecasts and warnings. ISRO supplies satellite data, and the Survey of India maps terrain.

questions.question: The National Highways Authority of India was set up to develop and maintain
questions.explanation: NHAI develops and manages the national highway network. Village roads fall to state and rural development agencies.

questions.question: A base line in chain surveying should be
options: The longest line, measured with the greatest care
questions.explanation: The base line controls the whole framework, so it is made as long as the ground allows and measured most carefully; errors in it propagate everywhere.

questions.question: Well-conditioned triangles in a chain survey framework have angles close to
questions.explanation: Near-equilateral triangles minimise the effect of a small angular error on the computed sides. Very acute or obtuse triangles amplify it.

questions.question: Which type of level uses a compensator instead of a bubble to level the line of sight?
questions.explanation: An automatic or self-levelling instrument uses a gravity-suspended compensator, so only rough levelling by the circular bubble is needed.

questions.question: The difference in level between two points is independent of
questions.explanation: Height difference is a property of the two points, so any correct route gives the same answer. That is exactly why a closed circuit reveals accumulated error.

questions.question: Contours on a map are most useful to a surveyor for
options: Computing earthwork volumes and planning alignments
questions.explanation: Contours give the ground shape, from which cut and fill quantities, gradients and drainage can all be derived.

questions.question: Setting the theodolite exactly over a station mark is called
questions.explanation: Centring places the vertical axis over the ground mark using a plumb bob or optical plummet, and is done before final levelling.

questions.question: If a traverse has a large closing error, the first thing to check is
options: The field measurements and booking for a gross mistake
The colour of the ink used
questions.explanation: A large misclosure indicates a blunder such as a transposed digit, a missed station or a wrongly read angle, not the small random errors that adjustment rules are meant to spread.

questions.question: Which of these is a limitation of GPS surveying?
options: Poor accuracy under dense tree canopy or between tall buildings
It cannot measure height at all
questions.explanation: GPS needs a clear sky view; canopy and buildings block or reflect signals. Height is measured, though less precisely than horizontal position.

questions.question: Coordinates recorded by a total station are usually stored as
questions.explanation: A total station works in a local rectangular system of northing, easting and reduced level, which can later be transformed to geographic coordinates.

questions.question: Georeferencing an aerial photograph means
options: Assigning real-world coordinates to its pixels
Printing it at a larger size
questions.explanation: Georeferencing ties image coordinates to ground coordinates using control points, so the image can be overlaid on a map.

questions.question: On a map, the representative fraction 1:1000 is a
questions.explanation: The smaller the denominator the larger the scale, so 1:1000 shows a small area in great detail while 1:50,000 covers much more ground with less.

questions.question: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed has magnitude only. Velocity, force and displacement all carry direction as well and are vectors.

questions.question: The principle used in a spirit level bubble is that
options: A bubble rises to the highest point of a curved sealed tube
questions.explanation: The tube is slightly curved, so the bubble, being lighter than the liquid, settles at the top, which is the middle only when the tube is horizontal.

questions.question: The average of 12, 15, 18 and 15 is
questions.explanation: The four values total 60, and 60 divided by 4 is 15.

questions.question: A field is 200 m long and 150 m wide. Its area in hectares is
questions.explanation: The area is 30,000 square metres, and one hectare is 10,000 square metres, so the field is 3 hectares.

questions.question: If the ratio of two numbers is 3:5 and their sum is 64, the larger number is
questions.explanation: Eight parts total 64, so one part is 8 and the larger number is five parts, or 40.

questions.question: Which format is most suitable for sharing a survey plan so the recipient cannot easily alter it?
questions.explanation: PDF fixes the layout and is not readily editable without special tools, which is why it is the standard for issuing drawings and reports.

questions.question: India's Green Revolution began in which decade?
questions.explanation: High-yielding wheat varieties were introduced from the mid-1960s, transforming output in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
